facts.claim: Results demonstrated some evidence consumers’ intentions to engage with athlete-related social media content were greater when this content was posted by an indirect source, rather than directly by the athlete.
facts.quote: Results demonstrated some evidence consumers’ intentions to engage with athlete-related social media content were greater when this content was posted by an indirect source, rather than directly by the athlete.

facts.claim: Content was perceived as more credible and less biased than when the same information was sent from the athlete directly.
facts.quote: This content was perceived as more credible and less biased than when the same information was sent from the athlete directly.

facts.claim: The type of source does not affect message credibility or CR but a corporate source generates more WOM.
facts.quote: Results showed that the type of source does not affect message credibility or CR but a corporate source generates more WOM.

facts.claim: Followers' perceived attractiveness of influencers, similarity to influencers, procedural fairness, and interpersonal fairness of their interactions with influencers are positively related to the strength of their parasocial relationship with influencers, which further mediates the effect of the aforementioned factors on followers’ interests in influencer-promoted products.
facts.quote: The results of an online survey showed that followers’ perceived attractiveness of influencers, similarity to influencers, procedural fairness, and interpersonal fairness of their interactions with influencers are positively related to the strength of their parasocial relationship with influencers, which further mediates the effect of the aforementioned factors on followers’ interests in influencer-promoted products.

facts.claim: The number of followers positively influences source attractiveness, source trustworthiness as well as purchase intention.
facts.quote: Furthermore, the results reveal that the number of followers positively influences source attractiveness, source trustworthiness as well as purchase intention.

research.angle: While parasocial relationships and similarity are linked to product interest, a higher follower count is linked to increased trustworthiness and purchase intention, and indirect sources can sometimes be perceived as more credible than direct ones.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that while interpersonal factors like similarity and fairness build parasocial relationships that drive interest, larger follower counts and third-party sources also play significant roles in credibility and purchase intent.
research.caveat: The study on parasocial relationships is an observational study showing associations rather than direct causation.
